result: The fix was a one-line off-by-one in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:16`: `index()` validated `page` from the query string (already 1-based, defaulting to 1 via `ListPostsQuerySchema`) and then passed `page + 1` to `Post.newQuery().paginate()`, so `/posts` read page 2 and no request could ever reach the newest ten posts; since `paginate()` from `@guren/core` derives the pager's `currentPage`, `from`/`to`, and first/last/prev/next links from the ORM result's own meta, correcting the query argument to `{ page, perPage: 10 }` also fixes the pager numbering and the highlighted page in one go — nothing about ordering, page size, or search was touched. I added `tests/PostsPagination.test.ts`, which migrates the test database, installs 25 posts under a dedicated author (cleaning up after itself), and asserts through the real Inertia response that `/posts` and `/posts?page=1` both return the 10 newest posts with meta `page 1 of 3, 1–10 of 25` and no `prev` link, that pages 1–3 together cover every post exactly once with `currentPage` matching the request, and that page 3 is the final 5 posts with `from: 21, to: 25` and no `next` link; all four fail against the original code and pass with the fix. `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` passes 6/6 (the `ValidationException` trace printed by the pre-existing `posts.search` test is unchanged, pre-existing log noise, not a failure).
